title: MCP protocol, OAuth and application integration capability ledger

rows.capability: MCP client connect, initialize and close
rows.operation: Create an `McpClient`, run the `initialize` handshake, expose connection state and server capabilities, and close the transport; closing must not wait for unrelated background work. The application layer wraps this as `McpServerConnection` with `connecting`, `connected`, `disconnected`, `needs-auth`, `failed` and `closed` states.
rows.consumer: Generic `McpClient` and application `McpServerConnection`/`McpSessionManager`; transport callers do not own JSON-RPC state themselves.

scenarios: closing while initialize is pending returns without waiting
closing while a token refresh is in flight does not wait for the refresh

rows.cppEvidence: `McpHttpSessionTest.cpp` and `McpStdioSessionTest.cpp` cover handshakes; `McpSessionIntegrationTest.cpp:237` asserts Pike resolves the connect phase before session creation. Pike has no background connect, retry/backoff or explicit pending-initialize close test; its assembly awaits every enabled server before returning.
rows.recommendation: Port the v1.3.0 `McpServerConnection` state/retry shape and make close abort a pending initialize and any refresh wait. Add a C++ test that starts a never-answering initialize, closes, and asserts prompt/creation does not block; distinguish close-during-connect from close-after-connected.

rows.capability: MCP tools/list pagination and naming
rows.operation: Follow `nextCursor` across pages, validate each tool, and assign order-independent `mcp__<server>__<tool>` names with the 64-character hash suffix on collisions.
rows.consumer: Application tool surface and codemode/tool_search catalogs; direct callers of `McpClient.listTools`.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpToolsListTest.cpp:118` covers pagination and a terminal null/empty cursor; `McpToolNameTest.cpp:38-57` covers sanitization and hash suffixes; `McpHttpSessionTest.cpp:321` covers a named HTTP listing. No v1.3.0 differential scenario is captured here.
rows.recommendation: Keep the implementation; add a public differential scenario only when the parity suite can name the same tool/cursor inputs. Do not fold tool naming into a generic JSON-RPC client test.

rows.capability: MCP tools/call arbitrary structured content
rows.operation: `tools/call` accepts `content` as an array of content blocks and `structuredContent` as any JSON value (array, primitive or null); a missing `content` defaults to `[]`, and `isError` is preserved.
rows.consumer: `McpClient.callTool`, the application tool wrapper, and codemode's script result channel.

sources: packages/mcp/test/client.test.ts:accepts structured content that is not an object
scenarios: client preserves an array structuredContent when content is absent
client preserves a primitive structuredContent
client preserves a null structuredContent
client and tool conversion preserve an error result

rows.cppEvidence: `McpToolsListTest.cpp:103` converts an object result with a `content` array. The converter rejects a missing/non-array `content` (`sent a tools/call result without content`), so a structured-only result accepted by v1.3.0 is a hard error in Pike; it does not test array, primitive or null `structuredContent`.
rows.recommendation: Accept an absent `content` as `[]`, validate arbitrary `structuredContent`, and add the captured array/primitive/null/error cases to the MCP result test. Keep `isError` separate from protocol errors.

rows.capability: MCP result conversion to model and script channels
rows.operation: Convert text/image/embedded-resource blocks to model content, render resource links and binary resources as pi text, middle-truncate combined text over 20 KiB with the output-file warning, and expose the full `CallToolResult` (minus `_meta`) to codemode separately from renderer details.
rows.consumer: Model-facing MCP tools, codemode nested calls, TUI renderers and the output-file spill path.

scenarios: tool conversion serializes structuredContent into model text
client and tool conversion preserve an error result

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/mcp/McpExtensionToolSource.cpp:convert_mcp_tools_call_result` (20 KiB middle truncation and temp file); `AgentMcpToolSurface` binds the result to `ExtensionToolResult.details`.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpToolsListTest.cpp:90` covers 20 KiB truncation and spill. Pike has one `details` JSON value (the whole CallToolResult) and no separate `structuredContent` channel or `{server,tool,fullOutputPath}` renderer details; resource links and binary resources are not rendered. This is a structural gap, not only a missing test.
rows.recommendation: Separate pi's `details` (`server`, `tool`, optional `fullOutputPath`) from the codemode script result (`structuredContent`) and port resource-link/binary placeholders. Add a conversion test whose inputs include array structuredContent and a resource link.

rows.capability: MCP resource listing, templates and reads
rows.operation: List resources and resource templates with pagination and read one resource by URI; resource operations use the same cancel/progress-capable request path as tools.
rows.consumer: Resource tools (`list_mcp_resources`, `list_mcp_resource_templates`, `read_mcp_resource`), management panels and codemode resource calls.

scenarios: connecting a server lists tools but not resources
resources are listed on demand after the connection is ready
a resources/list failure leaves the server connected and usable for tools

rows.cppEvidence: `McpResourceToolsTest.cpp:190-296` covers tool descriptions, cross-server pagination and cursors. In production `ProductionMcpConnection::refresh` calls `fetch_mcp_resource_snapshot` during connect and fails the connection if that snapshot fails; the manager also exposes `resource_count`, whereas v1.3.0 only sets `hasResources` and lists on demand.
rows.recommendation: Remove the connect-time resource snapshot; set `hasResources` from `initialize.capabilities.resources` and use the resource tools' on-demand pages. Keep a resource-list failure local to the resource call, as captured. This is a prerequisite for a reusable `cch_mcp` connection.

rows.capability: Codex-compatible MCP resource tools
rows.operation: Expose `list_mcp_resources`, `list_mcp_resource_templates` and `read_mcp_resource` with pi's descriptions, parameters, pagination and per-server failure collection at the widest non-hidden exposure.
rows.consumer: Application tool surface, codemode scripts and the `mcp_servers` prompt section.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpResourceToolsTest.cpp:190` checks verbatim descriptions/schemas; cross-server pagination and failure collection are covered. `McpSessionIntegrationTest.cpp:346` covers a live resource listing through a session.
rows.recommendation: Keep; add the captured resource-list failure case to the session test so the connection remains usable after a failed resource list.

rows.capability: Server-to-client roots/list and ping
rows.operation: A connected client answers server requests: `ping` returns `{}`, and `roots/list` returns the configured roots (pi passes `roots` into `McpClient` and installs the handler for both transports).
rows.consumer: MCP servers that probe roots or liveness; application connection adapters.
rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/mcp/McpHttpClient.cpp` installs `ping` and a `roots/list` handler that hardcodes `file://<cwd>`; `McpStdioClient` has no server-request handler at all.
rows.cppEvidence: No `McpProtocolSurfaceTest` case sends `roots/list` or `ping` through the stdio client. The HTTP handler ignores configured roots and derives the single root from the process cwd.
rows.recommendation: Carry roots on the connection (not process cwd) and install the same `ping`/`roots/list` handlers for stdio and HTTP. Add a test that sends both server requests on each transport.

rows.capability: MCP progress notifications and deadline re-arming
rows.operation: A request that supplies `onProgress` advertises `_meta.progressToken`; matching `notifications/progress` messages re-arm the request deadline and feed the progress callback.
rows.consumer: Tool execution updates and long-running MCP calls; the management/status display.
rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/mcp/McpHttpClient.cpp:with_progress_token,progress_token_of,send_request`; `McpStdioClient` progress callback; `McpProductionAdapters.cpp:AgentMcpToolSurface::register_tool` forwards progress to the run update sink.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpProgressTest.cpp:84` covers token injection and extraction; `McpHttpClient` has the re-arm/deadline path. Progress through stdio is not covered by the same test, and no v1.3.0 capture is present.
rows.recommendation: Add matched stdio/HTTP progress scenarios before marking verified; the current row is implementation-complete but unverified against the frozen capture.

rows.capability: MCP request cancellation and timeout
rows.operation: A cancelled or timed-out request sends `notifications/cancelled` with pi's reason (`Aborted`/`Request timed out`) and settles with the cancellation/timeout error; `initialize` is never cancellable.
rows.consumer: Agent turn cancellation and tool execution; HTTP/stdio transports.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpFailureIsolationTest.cpp:239` covers cancellation notification and connection reuse; `:269` covers a server that keeps streaming; `:293` covers an explicit timeout. The refresh-specific gap is tracked separately.
rows.recommendation: Retain; add the captured refresh-cancellation scenario as the differential case, because generic cancellation tests do not exercise the OAuth recovery path.

rows.capability: Cancellation during OAuth refresh never dispatches the request
rows.operation: When a request gets a 401 and the token refresh is in flight, aborting or timing out the request settles it immediately; once the refresh completes, the request must not be sent with the new token. The refresh itself may complete and persist rotated tokens.
rows.consumer: OAuth-eligible HTTP MCP calls; the application tool wrapper and Agent turn cancellation.

scenarios: cancelling a tool call during OAuth refresh never sends it after the refresh completes
a tool call that times out during OAuth refresh never sends it after the refresh completes

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/mcp/McpOAuthTokenResolver.cpp:current_headers`; `McpHttpClient.cpp:post` resolves headers before assigning `request.stop_token`; there is no shared in-flight refresh or refresh lock.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpOAuthSessionTest.cpp:548` proves rotated tokens are persisted before the request continues, but no test aborts during refresh. Pike blocks the caller in `current_headers` until refresh returns; the transport then observes the aborted stop token and suppresses the POST. Correct final dispatch, but not v1.3.0's immediate cancellation and shared-refresh semantics.
rows.recommendation: Make the refresh a shared background operation (per server/URL) that the request waits on only while not cancelled; on cancellation settle immediately, keep the refresh alive, and suppress dispatch. Add the captured abort and timeout cases, asserting exactly one 401 tool attempt and zero post-refresh calls.

rows.capability: Close does not refresh and reuses the last token
rows.operation: Closing an MCP HTTP connection aborts pending transport work, sends a best-effort session DELETE with the last token, never asks the auth provider for a new token, and never waits for a refresh.
rows.consumer: Application shutdown, `/mcp` disable/reconnect, and Agent session teardown.

scenarios: closing while a token refresh is in flight does not wait for the refresh

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/mcp/McpHttpClient.cpp:close` (DELETE + GET stream abort); `McpProductionAdapters.cpp:ProductionMcpConnection::close`; `McpOAuthTokenResolver` has no `settled()` equivalent.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpHttpSessionTest.cpp` covers session DELETE and close; `McpOAuthSessionTest.cpp` covers request-time refresh, but there is no close-during-refresh test. Pike's close is synchronous and does not wait for `McpOAuthTokenResolver` work, but it also has no token-settled contract to ensure a rotated refresh response is persisted before exit.
rows.recommendation: Add a token-provider `settled()`/in-flight tracking seam so close can skip starting a refresh while still allowing an already-answered refresh to persist. Test that close returns within a bounded time while `/token` is stalled and that DELETE carries the pre-refresh access token.

rows.capability: OAuth protected-resource and authorization-server discovery
rows.operation: Discover RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, then RFC 8414/OpenID authorization-server metadata in pi's candidate order, with loopback/http exceptions and issuer validation; discovery requests must be cancellable.
rows.consumer: Generic OAuth flow, sign-in and request-time refresh.

scenarios: cancellation during protected-resource discovery aborts the flow

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/mcp/McpOAuthDiscovery.{hpp,cpp}`; `McpOAuthFlow.cpp:authorize_mcp`; `OAuthHttpClient` requests use `std::stop_token{}` in discovery and flow.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpOAuthDiscoveryTest.cpp:55-182` covers path-suffixed retry, root-path behavior, candidate order and issuer mismatch. Discovery accepts no caller stop token, so a cancelled sign-in cannot abort a stalled discovery request.
rows.recommendation: Thread the sign-in/session cancellation token through discovery and flow requests. Add the captured stalled protected-resource case and assert the request socket is closed and no token/registration request follows.

rows.capability: OAuth dynamic registration, PKCE and sign-in callback
rows.operation: Register a client (or use a Client ID Metadata Document), build an S256 PKCE authorization URL, run the loopback/paste callback, exchange the code and persist tokens; cancellation while waiting for the browser or pasted URL must stop the flow.
rows.consumer: `signInMcpServer`/`/mcp login`, `McpOAuthFlow`, `OAuthCallbackServer`, `McpOAuthSignIn`.

scenarios: cancellation during dynamic client registration aborts the flow
cancellation while waiting for the browser callback stops sign-in
authorization response from another issuer is rejected before token exchange

rows.cppEvidence: `McpOAuthFlowTest.cpp:112` covers discovery/registration/authorization and `:164` the code exchange; `McpOAuthSignInTest.cpp:246-295` covers pasted and browser callbacks and CIMD. Neither flow nor sign-in takes a session stop token; the callback has a 300 s timer but no cancellation classification matching pi's callback expiry.
rows.recommendation: Thread cancellation through registration and the callback wait, and classify callback expiry as pi does. Add the captured registration-stall and prompt-cancel cases; assert no token request after cancellation.

rows.capability: OAuth token refresh, rotation and cross-process locking
rows.operation: Refresh tokens when the access token is near expiry or rejected, coalesce concurrent refreshes, rotate refresh tokens, persist before continuing, serialize across processes with a lock, and never loop on `invalid_grant`.
rows.consumer: `createMcpAuthProvider` in the application integration; `McpOAuthTokenResolver` for request-time credentials.

scenarios: cancelling a tool call during OAuth refresh never sends it after the refresh completes
a tool call that times out during OAuth refresh never sends it after the refresh completes

rows.cppEvidence: `McpOAuthFlowTest.cpp:203` covers rotated refresh persistence and `:238` a dead refresh token; `McpOAuthSessionTest.cpp:548` covers request-time rotation. Pike refreshes per request with a five-minute margin, no single-flight/coalescing and no cross-process lock; it does not have v1.3.0's 30-second skew.
rows.recommendation: Extract refresh into a per-server single-flight with pi's 30-second skew and a file lock; keep the no-loop `invalid_grant` rule. Add concurrent-401 and cross-process lock cases before claiming parity.

rows.capability: RFC 9207 issuer verification
rows.operation: When the authorization response carries `iss`, or the server advertises `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported`, reject a mismatched issuer before the token exchange.
rows.consumer: OAuth sign-in and refresh flows; callback parsing.

scenarios: authorization response from another issuer is rejected before token exchange

rows.cppEvidence: `McpOAuthFlowTest.cpp:9` states a code from another issuer must never reach the token endpoint; `McpOAuthDiscoveryTest.cpp:165` rejects a mismatched authorization-server issuer. The captured upstream exact error and zero-token-request observation is the comparison case.
rows.recommendation: Retain; add the captured forged-issuer scenario as the C++ differential case. Keep the check before token exchange and preserve the exact server/expected/received fields.

rows.capability: OAuth credential persistence in mcp-auth.json
rows.operation: Store client registration, tokens, expiry, PKCE state and discovery under `mcp__<server>|<url>` in `mcp-auth.json`, migrate legacy `auth.json` records, and remove credentials on sign-out.
rows.consumer: Application `McpOAuthCredentialStore`; `McpAuthStore`; `/mcp logout` and session startup.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpAuthStoreTest.cpp:66-214` covers key shape, legacy takeover, tokens, removal and migration; `McpOAuthSessionTest.cpp:485` covers the `mcp-auth.json` record. The C++ store is file-backed but has no cross-process refresh lock.
rows.recommendation: Keep the store; pair it with the refresh lock slice. Add a two-process refresh test before verified status.

rows.capability: Application MCP configuration and validation
rows.operation: Load `mcp.json` from the agent directory and a trusted project, validate server URLs (v1.3.0 accepts `http` and `https`, rejects other schemes), OAuth settings, exposure/toolExposure and timeout.
rows.consumer: `createMcpExtension`, `loadMcpConfig`, `McpSessionManager`, CLI `mcp` commands and the management panel.

scenarios: application config accepts http and https but rejects another scheme

rows.cppEvidence: `McpConfigSurfaceTest.cpp:154` matches v1.0.4 exposure cases; `McpHttpServerConfig.cpp:19` rejects every non-`https://` URL. The captured v1.3.0 rule accepts `http://` and `https://` and rejects `ftp://` with `url must be an http or https URL`.
rows.recommendation: Change only the MCP URL validation and transport gate; do not change the Magpie provider TLS contract. Add the captured scheme cases to `McpConfigSurfaceTest`.

rows.capability: Streamable HTTP transport: HTTP/HTTPS, redirects and TLS
rows.operation: POST JSON-RPC with `accept: application/json, text/event-stream`, accept JSON or SSE, capture `mcp-session-id`, follow standard fetch redirects (same-origin keeps Authorization, cross-origin strips it), accept plain HTTP and HTTPS, and retain platform TLS certificate validation.
rows.consumer: Generic `StreamableHttpTransport`; application `McpHttpClient`; OAuth-protected server calls.

scenarios: streamable HTTP transport connects over plain http
HTTPS transport connects when its certificate is trusted
HTTPS transport rejects an untrusted certificate
same-origin redirect is followed and keeps the request auth header
cross-origin redirect is followed without Authorization and is rejected

rows.cppEvidence: `McpHttpSessionTest.cpp:396` asserts an `http://` URL is rejected; `:445` asserts a redirect is refused with `never follows a redirect`. Pike has no plain-HTTP or redirect test because the behavior is intentionally absent. TLS trust is delegated to Boost.Asio/OpenSSL and tested only indirectly.
rows.recommendation: Remove the TLS-only registration gate and the redirect refusal; reuse the existing Boost.Beast/OpenSSL transport for `https` and add a plain-HTTP/StreamTransport variant or a minimal HTTP stream. Preserve certificate verification. Add the captured same/cross-origin redirect and self-signed trust cases.

rows.capability: MCP streamable HTTP session and server-to-client GET stream
rows.operation: Capture and echo `Mcp-Session-Id`, treat 404 with a session id as an expired session and retry once on a fresh session, open the long-lived GET stream after initialization, reconnect with the server's retry hint, and close the stream on shutdown.
rows.consumer: Generic HTTP transport; application manager; OAuth-protected calls.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpHttpGetStreamTest.cpp:338-387` covers 405 as feature-absent, retry hints and out-of-range hints; `McpHttpSessionTest.cpp` covers session headers and a 404 session expiry. No v1.3.0 capture is present.
rows.recommendation: Keep; add a matched capture when the frozen harness can exercise an SSE GET stream, including the retry hint and 405 case.

rows.capability: Request-time authentication and 401 handling
rows.operation: Attach configured headers or an auth provider's current token to every request; on 401 refresh once and retry with the new credentials; if authorization is required, surface the explicit OAuth re-login/needs-auth outcome instead of a silent unauthenticated retry.
rows.consumer: Generic HTTP transport and application `McpRequestAuthSource`/`McpAuthProvider`.

scenarios: streamable HTTP transport connects over plain http
same-origin redirect is followed and keeps the request auth header
cross-origin redirect is followed without Authorization and is rejected

rows.cppEvidence: `McpOAuthSessionTest.cpp:525` covers a stored token resolving without a token request; `McpFailureIsolationTest` and `McpHttpSessionTest` cover auth errors. Pike resolves headers per request but has no refresh single-flight and no test of request dispatch after a cancelled header refresh.
rows.recommendation: Keep per-request resolution and the explicit OAuth error, but pair it with the refresh single-flight/cancellation slice. Add the captured same-origin (auth preserved) and cross-origin (auth stripped) cases.

rows.capability: MCP exposure model and discovery activation
rows.operation: Classify servers and tools as `codemode`, `direct`, `deferred` or `hidden`; activate codemode/tool_search from configuration; re-register withdrawn tools as hidden; render the `mcp_servers` section with indirect exposure.
rows.consumer: `createMcpExtension`, `McpSessionManager`, codemode/tool_search, the system prompt section and the management panel.

scenarios: first prompt does not wait for a codemode server still initializing
first prompt waits startupWaitMs for a direct server and reports still connecting

rows.cppEvidence: `McpConfigSurfaceTest.cpp:227` covers exact-name-beats-pattern; `McpServersSectionTest.cpp:63-101` covers indirect listings and the deferred clause; `McpSessionIntegrationTest.cpp:214-282` covers codemode activation and the warning. Deferred exposure remains unreachable because Pike has no `tool_search`.
rows.recommendation: Keep the direct/codemode activation and section rendering. Decide `tool_search` membership or explicitly record deferred as unreachable; do not activate deferred tools without the discovery tool.

rows.capability: Application startup wait and background connection
rows.operation: At `session_start`, connect enabled servers in the background; the first prompt waits at most `startupWaitMs` (default 10 s) only for servers with direct tools, reports still-connecting servers, and never blocks on codemode/deferred servers.
rows.consumer: `createMcpExtension` session lifecycle, `before_agent_start`, the application Session, and the `/mcp` panel.

scenarios: first prompt does not wait for a codemode server still initializing
first prompt waits startupWaitMs for a direct server and reports still connecting
direct server tools become available when it connects within startupWaitMs

rows.cppEvidence: Pike's `McpSessionManager::start` awaits every enabled server serially before `session_start` completes; there is no `startupWaitMs`, no background connection and no still-connecting application notification. `McpSessionIntegrationTest.cpp:237` asserts the opposite (connect phase resolved before creation).
rows.recommendation: This is the largest application gap. Start connections asynchronously, keep a per-server ready promise and state, add the bounded first-prompt wait for direct servers and pi's notification, and make `/mcp` usable while connecting. Add a test with a never-answering direct server and one that connects inside the wait.

rows.capability: Application connection setup without eager resource listing
rows.operation: Connecting lists tools only; resources remain lazy and a failed `resources/list` does not fail the connection. `hasResources` comes from the initialize capability, not from a resource snapshot.
rows.consumer: `McpServerConnection`, `McpSessionManager`, resource tools and the session status surface.

scenarios: connecting a server lists tools but not resources
resources are listed on demand after the connection is ready
a resources/list failure leaves the server connected and usable for tools

rows.cppEvidence: `McpSessionManagerTest.cpp:727` seeds `resource_count_value`, implying the resource snapshot is part of the manager model; `ProductionMcpConnection::refresh` fails the connection when the snapshot fails. This is the v1.0.4 shape, not v1.3.0.
rows.recommendation: Remove the snapshot and `resource_count`; set `has_resources` from capabilities. Add the captured three cases to `McpSessionManagerTest`/`McpSessionIntegrationTest`.

rows.capability: MCP management UI and `/mcp` actions
rows.operation: `/mcp` lists servers and exposes sign-in, sign-out, reconnect, tools, exposure, enable/disable and project enable/disable actions; status stays readable while a server connects; actions produce explicable outcomes.
rows.consumer: TUI `McpManagerFlow`/`McpManagerPresenter`; CLI `mcp` commands; the live `McpSessionManager`.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpManagerFlowTest.cpp:461-504` covers menu open/navigation/reconnect and refresh on manager change; `McpManagerPresenterTest.cpp:232-283` covers state/projection and exposure/tools menus; `McpServerManagementTest.cpp` covers config. There is no frozen v1.3.0 management capture; current tests are v1.0.4-shaped.
rows.recommendation: Keep the panel; add differential cases for status while connecting, stale sign-in/reconnect outcomes and the `enable-project`/`disable-project` actions. Multi-candidate sign-in selection remains the known interaction gap.

rows.capability: Session tool registration and codemode routing
rows.operation: Register each MCP tool on the live session surface with its exposure, schemas, description and call binding; keep a withdrawn tool registered as hidden; forward model calls, arguments and progress; expose the result to codemode's nested-call channel.
rows.consumer: `AgentMcpToolSurface`, codemode `tools.*`, direct session tools and tool_search catalogs.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpSessionIntegrationTest.cpp:214-282` covers codemode registration/activation and a scripted call; `McpToolsListTest.cpp` covers naming/schema. No v1.3.0 differential capture.
rows.recommendation: Keep; the conversion gap stays separate. Add a differential case that calls a tool with array structuredContent from codemode and checks the script value/result channel.

rows.capability: MCP reconnect and tools/list_changed refresh
rows.operation: Reconnect a dead stdio/HTTP connection and refresh tools; `notifications/tools/list_changed` re-lists and re-registers, `notifications/resources/list_changed` refreshes resource state; a 404 session expiry retries once.
rows.consumer: `McpServerConnection`, `McpSessionManager`, `/mcp reconnect`, and the live tool surface.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpSessionManagerTest.cpp:371-391` covers tools/list failure and healthy registration; `McpSessionManagerTest.cpp:771` dispatches `resources/list_changed`; HTTP session expiry retry is in `ProductionMcpConnection::request`. No stdio/HTTP reconnect differential capture.
rows.recommendation: Keep; add re-list/reconnect cases with a dropped transport and a changed tool list. The external sign-in pickup is a separate gap.

rows.capability: Cancellation through OAuth discovery, registration and sign-in
rows.operation: Cancelling a sign-in or refresh aborts discovery/registration/token requests and the browser/paste wait; the cancelled flow does not continue to authorization or token exchange.
rows.consumer: `authorizeMcp`, `signInMcpServer`, `OAuthCallbackServer` and the TUI/CLI sign-in prompt.

scenarios: cancellation during protected-resource discovery aborts the flow
cancellation during dynamic client registration aborts the flow
cancellation while waiting for the browser callback stops sign-in

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/mcp/McpOAuthFlow.cpp`, `McpOAuthDiscovery.cpp`, `McpOAuthSignIn.cpp`, `OAuthCallbackServer.cpp`: all HTTP calls use `std::stop_token{}` and no sign-in stop token is threaded through.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpOAuthSignInTest.cpp:246-295` covers callback/paste success but no cancellation; `McpOAuthFlowTest.cpp` covers successful discovery/registration. Pike's flow has a 300 s timer but no caller-cancellation propagation, so a stalled discovery/registration keeps running after the session ends.
rows.recommendation: Thread an `AbortSignal` equivalent through the whole flow and callback wait; classify callback expiry as pi does. Add the three captured cancellation cases, asserting the stalled request is aborted and token requests remain zero.

rows.capability: Pick up sign-ins performed outside the session
rows.operation: At each turn start, compare stored MCP tokens with the snapshot at sign-in and reconnect a server whose credentials changed outside the session (for example `pi mcp login` in another process).
rows.consumer: `createMcpExtension` `turn_start`/`reconnectSignedIn`, `McpServerConnection`, `mcp-auth.json`.
rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/runtime/McpSessionManager` has no per-turn token snapshot or external-sign-in hook; only its own sign-in action reconnects.
rows.cppEvidence: No C++ test covers an external `mcp-auth.json` change between turns. The manager reconnects only through `/mcp` or a failed call.
rows.recommendation: Add a per-turn token fingerprint check on the manager and reconnect a server whose stored tokens changed. Test with an in-memory store mutated from a second handle.

rows.capability: Stdio failure diagnostics
rows.operation: Keep the last 2000 characters of a failed stdio server's stderr and surface them with the failure.
rows.consumer: `McpServerConnection.stderrTail`, the management panel and failure messages.
rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/runtime/McpProductionAdapters.cpp` checks `transport.stderr.trim()` for `StdioTransport`, but `McpStdioClient` drains stderr to `/dev/null`; `McpLiveConnection::stderr_tail` is always absent.
rows.cppEvidence: `McpSessionManagerTest.cpp:371` asserts a failed server reports the stderr tail, but the production adapter has no source for it. This is a code gap masked by a scripted test.
rows.recommendation: Capture a 64 KiB ring in `McpStdioClient` and expose it through `ProductionMcpConnection`. Add a real child-process failure test; do not rely on the scripted fake.

rows.capability: Deferred exposure and `tool_search`
rows.operation: A `deferred` server's tools stay undeclared until `tool_search` loads them for the next model call; activation of `deferred` activates `tool_search`, not codemode.
rows.consumer: MCP exposure policy, `tool_search`, the `mcp_servers` section and the model tool set.

scenarios: tool_search ranks a deferred tool, loads it through control.addTools, and the next call runs it
an unrelated tool_search query loads nothing and leaves the offered set unchanged

rows.cppEvidence: `McpSessionIntegrationTest.cpp` reproduces both captured scenarios through the public `AgentSession::prompt`: a `deferred` server's tools stay out of the offered set until `tool_search` loads the single ranked match with the frozen text `Loaded 1 tool. They are available from your next call:\n- mcp__echo__echo: Echo the incoming text back.`, the next request executes it, and a no-match search returns `No matching tools found.` with an unchanged offered set. Repeated searches in one run load the next-ranked match each time without re-announcing a loaded tool (pi's two-search ordering case in `packages/durable/test/tool-search.test.ts`). The loadout is a persisted `SystemMessage.tools_added` record: the fork case runs `echo` in one branch and the erroring `fail` in the other and both keep their own set across reopen, and the ordering case reopens the same session three times to load `slow`, `hang` and `crash` in rank order. `ToolSearchTest.cpp` covers the ranking seam directly.
rows.recommendation: Keep deferred tools undeclared until `tool_search` loads them, keep the loadout in the session transcript so forks and resumes replay their own set, and keep an extension tool's execute copyable per call because a model searches and calls tools more than once.
rows.notes: C++ covers the two captured scenarios, the frozen two-search ordering case and the durable loadout. `ExtensionToolRegistry::convert_extension_tool` now copies the extension execute per model call, so a registered `tool_search`, `codemode` or MCP tool stays callable for the whole session (it previously consumed the move-only operation on the first call).
